MCP adoption (a 1,847-server census finds 52% abandoned, 31% lightly maintained and only 17% production-grade, median server at 6 lifetime commits last touched 142 days ago; 97M monthly SDK downloads against 37,000–95,000 low-signal listings; the stateless revision starts breaking sessions in practice)

Agent execution control (CAGE proves certifying the categorical and numerical channels of a tool return separately does not compose; Cloudflare previews human-out-of-the-loop lifecycle and agent access controls; agentgateway named as the enterprise chokepoint where model access, tool calls and MCP servers get one policy)

Agent identity & authorization (CAGE certifies runtime permission decisions over a declared neighbourhood of one binding fault plus bounded numerical drift; Cequence ships Agent Personas binding an agent's job description to its model, tools and guardrails; the MCP spec finalises OAuth 2.1/OIDC auth)

Tool-use standards (schema-formatted tool specifications themselves weaken a model's internal refusal signals — judging against flattened text lifts refusal on harmful requests 23.8%→70.6% and drops prompt-injection success 25.6%→2.5%; UCP, ACP and MCP mapped as three competing agent-commerce camps)

MCP security (82% of 2,614 audited MCP implementations are path-traversal vulnerable and 30+ CVEs landed in 60 days; stored prompt injection framed as the return of an injection class the industry spent twenty years closing; Mem0 separates persistent memory-layer injection from context-window injection)
MCP adoption & the 2026-07-28 final spec (C# SDK 2.0 migration guide, stateless HTTP as a different programming model, MCPJam's caniuse.dev compatibility matrix across 15 clients)

Agent execution control (Embabel's GOAP engine replans at runtime when tool calls fail; SonarSource hires to build circuit breakers that reroute when acceptance rates drop; Kandou makes controlled inference and HITL checkpoints a hard requirement)

Agent identity & authorization (the final MCP spec binds client credentials to their issuing authorization server, deprecates DCR for Client ID Metadata Documents and mandates iss validation — but none of the six authorization SEPs touch scope selection)
Tool-use & agent-UI standards (700+ compatibility checks across 15 MCP clients, AG-UI vs A2UI vs OpenUI protocol soup, Data Turnstile function-calling data pipeline)
MCP & tool-surface security (SafeKeep shows JSON tool schemas weaken the refusal signal, 23.8% → 70.6%; memory-write path named as the real trust boundary)

Agent execution control (Shieldstral takes a plain-language policy at inference time instead of a fine-tune per policy change; the trajectory-assurance position paper argues sequences of individually permissible actions can still violate a system's invariants; LongHorizon-Harness keeps task state outside execution behind a read-only auditor)

Agent identity & authorization (Snowflake takes agent identity to GA beside a data-exfiltration prevention layer; Zero Networks makes just-in-time MFA per agent the unit of least privilege — least-privilege for non-human identities is now the shipped architecture)

MCP & tool-surface security (two independent Show HN launches the same day — signed deny-receipts for tool calls and default-deny egress caging for untrusted servers; an MCP server reframed as a supply-chain artifact you grant the right to act, not an endpoint you read from)

MCP adoption & the 2026-07-28 spec (a Swiss private bank writes 'standards such as the Model Context Protocol' into a job description as a delivery requirement; Snowflake ships the enforcement point at the warehouse boundary rather than the protocol; a 25-year SAP integrator benchmarks MCP against RFC/PI-PO/BTP)

Tool-use & agent-UI standards (ScrambleToolBench strips the semantic cues out of tool schemas so agents must discover behaviour by interaction — and finds successful discovery does not transfer to robust adaptation; the MCP/A2A boundary drawn through division of labour rather than spec comparison)

Agent identity & authorization (the pre-DNS HOSTS file as the analogy — a hand-maintained name-to-address list that worked only while everyone could be vouched for by reputation, which is exactly where agent identity sits; a paper binds agent identity to model weights cryptographically; the Ninth Circuit answers the attribution question from the other end by holding the *user*, not the vendor, is the one accessing)

MCP & tool-surface security (Enkrypt scanned 268,000 tools across 25,000 MCP servers in two months and found 143,000 vulnerabilities affecting 73% of them — not a long tail, the default state of the ecosystem agents connect to; the 28 July stateless core solved deployment scale and deferred authorization to extensions, and this is the intervening gap measured)

MCP adoption & the 2026-07-28 spec (no MCP or A2A spec news at all today — the news collector's own theme balance records a zero — and the protocol surfaces instead through its consequences: a stateless core with authorization deferred to extensions, a Medium piece arguing shell-out-to-CLI versus protocol-mediated tool access is still a live debate, and 143k vulnerabilities in the server population)

Tool-use & agent-UI standards (SkillTrace makes skill composition an explicit graph traversal; the 28 July extensions framework lets Tasks and MCP Apps ship without touching a core that is now stateless; and the day's LinkedIn argument is that neither A2A nor MCP will supply the governance layer between them)

Agent identity & authorization (Snowflake's Cortex AI Gateway ships with seven identity partners - 1Password, Aembit, Cyera, Linx, Okta, SailPoint, Saviynt - which is the identity industry collectively deciding the agent is the principal; NIST's AI Agent Standards Initiative is now the operative agent-identity workstream after the consortium dropped 'safety' from its name)

MCP & tool-surface security (the first large-scale dynamic audit of internet-facing MCP servers puts 380 of 414 with no authentication at all and hundreds exposing unauthenticated shell execution - and the gap is structural, because the finalized 2026-07-28 spec removed protocol-level sessions and pushed authorization out into extensions; the same author notes the ecosystem tests conformance and security but never load)

MCP adoption & the 2026-07-28 stateless rewrite (the biggest change since launch - sessions and the Mcp-Session-Id header are gone so any instance behind an ordinary load balancer answers any request, Tasks moves to an extension, Roots/Sampling/Logging are deprecated, and the SDKs have passed 1B cumulative downloads; Snowflake governs 100+ MCP servers, Salesforce ships Tableau MCP, ServiceNow GAs Action Fabric's MCP server, and a business-aviation employer writes MCP into a JD)

Tool-use & interop standards (A2A passes 150 organisations with v1.0 stable and native integration across Google, Microsoft and AWS, while the decision framework doing the rounds names the actual trade - plain APIs when the caller knows what it wants, MCP when the model must discover capability at runtime, A2A when the counterparty is itself non-deterministic, and MCP buys discovery at the price of a much larger, less predictable trust surface)

Tool-use & discovery standards (The Bitter Lesson of Tool Calling applies a Sutton-style argument to tool use — hand-engineered tool schemas, routers and selection heuristics lose to scale and general learning, cutting directly against the tool-registry and description-engineering layers most MCP-era agent stacks are building; two practitioner pieces settle MCP-vs-A2A as division of labour, A2A for delegation and MCP for tools and data)
